known.title: The recorded user choice to merge with `--delete-branch` deletes the local and remote plan branch while the merge question explicitly leaves that deletion out, so a branch delete runs without explicit user confirmation.
known.locator: Research, User choices, entry 2 (line 74); Research, Landing design, item 10 (line 63); Steps, row 1 manager_landing (line 82)
known.summary: User-form choice whose effect breaks a repository instruction file at repo_ref. Evidence: AGENTS.md:154 at 2cbd9b1 says "Don't perform destructive git operations (force-push, hard reset, branch delete) without explicit user confirmation". The gh manual (https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_pr_merge) documents `-d, --delete-branch` as "Delete the local and remote branch after merge". Scenario: the plan writes into the shipped contract that the merge runs `gh pr merge ... --match-head-commit <sha>` plus `--delete-branch` (Landing design item 10, carried out by step:manager_landing), and the choice states that the merge question keeps its two options `Merge now` / `Leave pull request open` and does not list the deletion. On `Merge now` the user confirmed only the merge, yet gh deletes both the remote and the local `plan-<issue>` branch: a branch delete without explicit confirmation. Main's v4 contract agrees (Checks and merge: the `Merge now` option must state the teardown, including the local branch delete with `git branch -d <branch>`). The recorded user preference for a short question does not outrank AGENTS.md (plan-reviewer Precedence). Fix: drop `--delete-branch`, or make the `Merge now` option name the local and remote branch deletion so that the answer confirms it, and delete the local branch with `git branch -d` (which refuses unmerged work) rather than a silent flag.

known.title: Acceptance A14 is the only check of the pull-request create-or-update outcome, but its grep for `Closes #<issue>` in the manager skill already passes at repo_ref, so it cannot fail without the change.
known.locator: Acceptance, A14 (line 104); Goal (line 5); Research, Landing design, item 6 (line 59)
known.summary: Evidence: at 2cbd9b1, plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/SKILL.md already contains `Closes #<issue>` at lines 222 and 224 (the `## Landing` paragraphs about the user-run closing pull request), so `grep -c 'Closes #<issue>' .../plan-manager/SKILL.md` prints 2 before any change and meets the row's Expected "Prints 1 or more". The Goal (line 5) requires that the manager create or update the pull request that closes the plan issue, implemented by Landing design item 6 (`gh pr list --head`, `gh pr edit --body-file`, `gh pr create --base --head --body-file`). Every other Goal outcome row (A12, A13, A15, A16, A17) fails at repo_ref (each grep prints 0 or 18 lines today), but no row checks `gh pr create` or `gh pr edit`, and A1's Expected is only "Exit 0". If step:manager_landing omits item 6 or the update path, every Acceptance row still passes. Fix: replace A14 with a check that fails today, for example `grep -c -e 'gh pr create' -e 'gh pr edit'` on plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/references/plan-contract.md (0 at repo_ref) or a pinned and mutation-tested clause for item 6 in scripts/tests/plan-skill-phases.mjs.

protected.summary: Request correction: the user asked to "commit and push its reviewed branch"; the plan instead commits the candidate on `plan-<issue>` before each code-review round (after the Acceptance commands and pre-commit checks pass), reviews the committed range `git diff $(git merge-base <remote>/<default> HEAD) HEAD`, and pushes only the head that the last `Code-review: pass` reviewed; any later change is a new commit with a new round. Sound: premises hold at 2cbd9b1: plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/SKILL.md:128-136 builds the review diff only from dirty paths (`git status --porcelain`, `git diff`, `git diff --cached`, `git diff --no-index /dev/null`), so commits already on a branch escape review; SKILL.md:144-146 lets MEDIUM/LOW fixes skip re-review, so a commit made after review can carry unreviewed bytes; https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_pr_merge documents `--match-head-commit <SHA>` ("Commit SHA that the pull request head must match to allow merge"). The real #19 reviews found exactly these gaps (code review round 1 advisory fixes after pass, round 2 reused-branch commits outside the dirty-tree diff, round 3 net merge-base diff and head revalidation). Respects the rules: commits stay local until the pass; they follow the Acceptance run and the pre-commit gate that AGENTS.md:142-143 asks for; no force-push (Do not touch); v3 Landing rules (Closes # in body, default-branch base, archive as verifier) stay intact; main's v4 contract does the same (Code-review rounds: commit the candidate before each round, full diff since the merge base; Checks and merge: `--match-head-commit <reviewed-head-sha>`). Steps still achieve the Goal: the reviewed head is pushed and merged only after the merge question.

Request correction: the user asked to "wait for CI"; the plan waits up to five minutes for the first check (`gh pr view --json statusCheckRollup`), then `gh pr checks <pr> --watch` over every reported check (not only `--required`), requires each `bucket` to be `pass` or `skipping`, ends a wait still pending after 60 minutes by leaving the PR open, and, when no check appears, says in the merge question that no CI ran and cites the passing Acceptance results. Sound: plan-lifecycle is shipped plugin payload for other repositories (AGENTS.md:26; plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/SKILL.md:165 at 2cbd9b1), which may have no workflow, a path-filtered workflow, or no required check; https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_pr_checks documents `--watch` ("Watch checks until they finish"), `--required` ("Only show checks that are required"), the `bucket` values pass/fail/pending/skipping/cancel and exit 8 for pending; https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_pr_view lists `statusCheckRollup`; the GitHub status-checks page says a skipped job reports success. It fixes the real #19 code-review findings (round 1 HIGH: `gh pr checks --watch --required` exits at once when checks have not appeared or none are required; round 3 MEDIUM: no terminal policy for a path-filtered or delayed workflow). Breaks no rule: the merge still needs a fresh `ask`, failed or cancelled checks block it, GitHub still enforces required checks server-side, and main's v4 contract prescribes the same policy (Checks and merge: wait up to five minutes for checks to appear, wait for every check, with no configured checks use the green local gate and say so in the merge question).

User: the user chose to keep `plan.mjs` and `scripts/tests/plan-cli.mjs` unchanged and to run landing as `git`/`gh` commands from the skill text, with no helper command that enforces their order. Sound: at 2cbd9b1 `archive` already accepts only a merged pull request into the default branch whose closing keyword closed the issue (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/references/plan-contract.md:266-292; plan-manager/SKILL.md:178-188), so a lifecycle-made PR with `Closes #<issue>` in its body archives without helper changes; GitHub enforces the reviewed head server-side through `gh pr merge --match-head-commit` (https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_pr_merge); nothing in plan.mjs states the zero-commit or user-landing rule, so no reader of the changed text lives there. Breaks no rule: no instruction file requires landing in the helper (AGENTS.md:100-101 keeps plan.mjs as the only lifecycle tool, which stays true; the preflight already uses `gh` commands directly in skill text), the v3 contract's Enforcement boundary says CLI silence certifies nothing and grants no permission, and main's v4 contract also runs landing as `gh`/`git` commands in skill text with `archive` as verifier. A3 keeps plan-cli.mjs as a regression check, and the Steps still achieve the Goal.
